title: Rigidified Poincare classification of dual abelian homomorphisms
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A,B$ be abelian varieties [def-sc-abelian-variety] with group-scheme structures [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $D_A,D_B$ be normalized dual Poincare data [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum], with universal invertible modules $P_A,P_B$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and identity-axis rigidifications $r_A,r_B$. For morphisms $f:A\to B$ and $g:D_B\to D_A$, define $\operatorname{ClassifiesAbelianDualHom}(D_A,D_B,f,g)$ to mean that there is an equality of morphisms $(f\times1)\circ e_{A,D_B}=e_{B,D_B}$ and an isomorphism $(1\times g)^*P_A\simeq(f\times1)^*P_B$ whose restriction to the identity axis, followed by the pullback of $r_B$, is the pullback of $r_A$ along $g$. Here $e_{A,T}=(0_A,1_T)$; all pullbacks are module inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. The pullback of a rigidification across any specified commutative square is defined by composing the canonical pullback composition comparison, transport along the square equality, the inverse composition comparison, the pullback of the given rigidification, and the pullback-of-unit comparison. The equality witness and isomorphism are existentially quantified: this is a predicate on the given maps, not an existence or uniqueness theorem for a dual map.
